reasons: Deviation classification is correct: p0149 is a blanket bar on Licensee assignment with no Affiliate/M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard on Licensor's consent, and p0134 makes Licensee's Change of Control an automatic termination event absent Licensor consent — both expressly walk-away under ASSIGN, so the clause meets neither preferred nor fallback (fallback requires mutual assignment to successors on notice).

Direction is correct for our side (we are Licensee/Customer): the edit expands our assignment rights, imposes a reciprocal reasonable-consent standard on Licensor, bars assignment to our competitors, and strips the Vendor's change-of-control exit right — exactly the redline guidance (add affiliate/successor carve-out; delete CoC termination right).

Edits are internally consistent: p0149's retained cross-reference to the Change Of Control section still works because the rewritten Article XX(a) now affirmatively provides no consent/termination right, and the trailing "CHANGE OF CONTROL" definition lead-in is preserved.

Failed minimal-edit heuristics (0.747 / 0.810 changed-character ratios) are not disqualifying here: neutralizing an automatic-termination-on-change-of-control provision and converting a one-sided prohibition into a carve-out plus reciprocal consent standard necessarily requires rewriting those sentences; no gratuitous unrelated changes were made.

Comment is accurate, concise, in the required first-person-plural tone with the [Playbook] prefix, states what changed and why, cites the walk-away positions, and concedes Licensor's residual consent right — an appropriate negotiating posture without lecturing.
No double-flagging: the Article XXII right of first refusal is expressly left to a separate rule, and severity (high) matches the rule.
